chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from 'Abdullah ibn Mighfal, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When you pray a part of the prayer during travel at a time other than its proper time, it will not harm you.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray travel prayers at times other than their usual times?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of prayer timing during travel, addressing the juristic debate on whether praying a specific prayer (e.g., Dhuhr) outside its canonical window while on a journey invalidates the act. It underscores the principle of *rukhsah* (divine concession), ensuring that travelers are not penalized for temporal adjustments necessitated by the hardships of travel, thereby reinforcing the ease (*yusr*) intended by Shariah for those in transit.
